dax_measures.name: YearTable (calculated table)
dax_measures.expression:
YearTable = 
VAR MinYear = CALCULATE(YEAR(MIN(fact_games[release_date])), ALL(fact_games))
VAR MaxYear = CALCULATE(YEAR(MAX(fact_games[release_date])), ALL(fact_games))
RETURN
SELECTCOLUMNS(
    GENERATESERIES(MinYear, MaxYear, 1),
    "Year", [Value],
    "IsPartialYear", [Value] = MaxYear
)
dax_measures.description: A lightweight year-grain table (not a daily calendar — every temporal requirement here operates at year grain). IsPartialYear is TRUE only for the final year in the range, since the data ends mid-year (2019-05-01). Relationship: YearTable[Year] (1) → fact_games[release_year] (*), single direction.

dax_measures.name: Total Games
dax_measures.description: Counts fact_games, not game_genres — the bridge table fans out (76,462 rows for 27,075 games), so counting it directly would overcount. Correctly cross-filters from a genre slicer because the fact_games ↔ game_genres relationship is bidirectional.

dax_measures.name: Average Price (Paid)
dax_measures.expression:
Average Price (Paid) = 
CALCULATE(
    AVERAGE(fact_games[price]),
    fact_games[is_free] = FALSE
)
dax_measures.description: Excludes $0 titles — blending them in would understate what a typical paid game costs. Validated: $6.71. A companion measure Average Price (All) = AVERAGE(fact_games[price]) exists as a secondary measure showing how much free titles pull the average down.

dax_measures.name: Positive Review Rate
dax_measures.expression:
Positive Review Rate = 
DIVIDE(
    SUM(fact_games[positive_ratings]),
    SUM(fact_games[total_ratings])
)
dax_measures.description: Ratio of sums, not AVERAGE() of the per-game rate column. Averaging the rate directly would weight a 3-review game the same as a 500,000-review game — this is why raw positive_ratings/negative_ratings are kept as additive columns in Gold.

dax_measures.name: Free-to-Play Ratio
dax_measures.expression:
Free-to-Play Ratio = 
DIVIDE(
    CALCULATE(COUNTROWS(fact_games), fact_games[is_free] = TRUE),
    COUNTROWS(fact_games)
)
dax_measures.description: Percentage of games that are free-to-play. Validated: 9.5%.

dax_measures.name: Genre Market Share
dax_measures.expression:
Genre Market Share = 
VAR GamesInGenre = COUNTROWS(fact_games)
VAR TotalGamesInContext = CALCULATE(COUNTROWS(fact_games), REMOVEFILTERS(game_genres))
RETURN DIVIDE(GamesInGenre, TotalGamesInContext)
dax_measures.description: Share of whatever is currently filtered — only the genre filter itself is removed. Makes cross-filtering by year or price tier meaningful. Genres are multi-label (85% of games carry more than one), so shares do not sum to 100% — never chart this as a pie or donut; use a horizontal bar chart. Validated: Action, no other filters active ≈ 43.96%.

dax_measures.name: YoY Release Growth
dax_measures.expression:
YoY Release Growth = 
VAR CurrentYear = SELECTEDVALUE(YearTable[Year])
VAR IsPartial = SELECTEDVALUE(YearTable[IsPartialYear])
VAR CurrentYearGames = COUNTROWS(fact_games)
VAR PriorYearGames = 
    CALCULATE(
        COUNTROWS(fact_games),
        REMOVEFILTERS(YearTable),
        YearTable[Year] = CurrentYear - 1
    )
RETURN
IF(
    ISBLANK(CurrentYear) || IsPartial,
    BLANK(),
    DIVIDE(CurrentYearGames - PriorYearGames, PriorYearGames)
)
dax_measures.description: Returns BLANK() for 2019 — the dataset's final year is a partial period (through 2019-05-01), and a growth % comparing 4 months to 12 months isn't a real rate. DIVIDE's blank-safe behavior also handles 1997 (no 1996) without a separate guard. Validated: 2018 → 28.4%, 2017 → 45.8%, 2019 → blank.

dax_measures.name: Price Tier Sort (supporting column)
dax_measures.description: Text sorts alphabetically by default (AAA, Budget, Free...). This calculated column, set via Column tools → Sort by Column, forces the price tier axis into logical price order.

dax_measures.name: % Windows / % Mac / % Linux (platform evolution)
dax_measures.expression:
% Windows = DIVIDE(CALCULATE(COUNTROWS(fact_games), fact_games[has_windows] = TRUE), COUNTROWS(fact_games))
% Mac     = DIVIDE(CALCULATE(COUNTROWS(fact_games), fact_games[has_mac]     = TRUE), COUNTROWS(fact_games))
% Linux   = DIVIDE(CALCULATE(COUNTROWS(fact_games), fact_games[has_linux]   = TRUE), COUNTROWS(fact_games))
dax_measures.description: % Windows sits essentially flat near 100% across the whole timeline (only 5 non-Windows games in the catalog) — that's correct, not a broken chart. The real signal in platform evolution is the Mac/Linux trajectory.

data_model_notes:
The Power BI data model consists of three tables:

1. fact_games (27,075 rows): one row per Steam appid, containing name, developer, publisher, release_date/year, price, price_tier (Free/Budget/Standard/Premium/AAA), is_free, positive_ratings, negative_ratings, total_ratings, positive_review_rate, achievements, owners_min/max/avg (estimated bucket midpoints), and has_windows/has_mac/has_linux booleans.

2. game_genres (76,462 rows, 29 distinct genres): a bridge table linking games to genres. 85% of games carry multiple genres, so genre shares do not sum to 100%.

3. YearTable (23 rows, 1997-2019): a calculated dimension built with GENERATESERIES. Contains a boolean IsPartialYear flag that is TRUE only for 2019.

Relationships:
• fact_games (1) ↔ game_genres (*) — bidirectional filtering, so a genre slicer correctly filters fact_games KPIs.
• YearTable[Year] (1) → fact_games[release_year] (*) — single direction, standard dimension-filters-fact pattern.
